Aakash Chopra Questions Team Management Strategy Regarding Vaibhav Suryavanshi

01 Nov 2026, 10:33 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bhaskar.com

2 min read

Context of Team Selection

Former Indian opening batsman Aakash Chopra has publicly questioned the team management's decision to exclude young talent Vaibhav Suryavanshi from the playing XI during the fourth T20 international against New Zealand.

Suryavanshi had previously been included in the squad for the second and third T20Is as a replacement for the injured Ishan Kishan. Following Kishan's return to fitness for the fourth match, Suryavanshi was dropped from the lineup.

Chopra’s Observations

In his analysis shared on his YouTube channel, Chopra raised concerns regarding the consistency of the team's selection policy. Key points from his commentary include:

  • Clarification of Roles: Chopra questioned whether Suryavanshi is only viewed as an injury replacement rather than a core part of the team's future roadmap.
  • Strategic Vision: He called upon the team management to articulate their long-term vision for the young player, noting that the rationale behind dropping him remains unclear to observers.
  • Development Advice: Chopra suggested that if the management cannot guarantee regular opportunities for the youngster in the national side, they should encourage him to focus on domestic first-class cricket to continue his development.

Match Outcome and Context

The fourth T20I resulted in an 87-run defeat for India, which is reported as their largest margin of defeat against New Zealand in the T20 format. Despite this loss, India holds a 3-1 lead in the five-match series.

  • Ishan Kishan's Performance: Upon returning to the side, Kishan was dismissed for a duck, caught by Jacob Duffy.
  • Upcoming Fixtures: The fifth and final match of the T20 series is scheduled for November 1.

Verification

Readers can verify these team selection details and match results by consulting official scorecards and statements released by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) or official broadcasting portals covering the India tour of New Zealand.
